states.edition: Alabama Energy and Residential Codes (ADECA): 2015 IRC as modified by Ala. Admin. Code r. 305-2-4-.09; adoption authority moved to the Home Builders Licensure Board on Oct 1, 2024 (Act 2024-443)
states.differs_from_app: Our row says 2021 IRC since 2023 and treats Alabama as a statewide IRC state. The state-level residential code on record (ADECA rule 305-2-4-.09, last supplemented 9/30/17) is the 2015 IRC with Alabama changes, and it is enforced only where local governments run permit programs. Since Oct 1, 2024 the Home Builders Licensure Board adopts the Alabama Residential Building Code; from Jan 1, 2027 builders must follow that code or the local code, but the edition the Board adopted is not published on its site. Big jurisdictions set their own: Birmingham 2021 IRC; unincorporated Mobile County 2024 IRC from July 1, 2026. Suggest kind "local".
notes: From Jan 1, 2027 a home builder must build to the Board-adopted Alabama Residential Building Code or, where one exists, the local residential code (Ala. Code 34-14A-12.1).

Local residential codes in effect on Jan 1, 2027 are not superseded; local codes adopted later must meet the state building and energy code minimums (and may not exceed the state energy code without cause).
Where no local code exists, the Board applied the 2015 IRC in its investigations for contracts signed on or after Feb 13, 2022.
ADECA's 2015 IRC modifications change no deck, stair or guard sections, so IRC values (36 in guard, 7-3/4 in riser, 10 in tread) stand.
Unincorporated Mobile County requires ASCE 7-22 wind speeds (160 mph Risk Category II minimum) and engineered or WFCM plans for dwellings.

states.edition: 2018 Kentucky Residential Code, Third Edition (Aug 2024): the 2015 IRC with Kentucky amendments, 815 KAR 7:125
states.differs_from_app: Our row says the KRC is based on the 2018 IRC, in force since 2019, with a 2021-based KRC in adoption. The 2018 KRC is based on the 2015 IRC. Its 2018 amendment took effect Aug 22, 2018, and the current Third Edition took effect Dec 3, 2024. The regulation shows no 2021-based KRC; its only pending item is that same Third Edition. Kentucky also amends stairs: 8-1/4 in max riser and 9 in min tread, not the IRC's 7-3/4 and 10.
notes: The KRC is a mini/maxi code: local governments may not adopt or enforce any other code for one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses.
Permits, inspections and certificates of occupancy are not required for a single-family dwelling unless a local ordinance requires them (815 KAR 7:125 Section 2(2)).
Statewide Table R301.2(1): Vult 115 mph in every county, weathering severe, termite moderate to heavy; ground snow 15 or 20 psf by county.
Frost depth (Table R403.1.4) is 24 in in most counties; 27–33 in for listed eastern and northern counties (e.g. Kenton, Boone, Campbell 30 in).
Seismic Design Category is set by county (Table R301.2.2.1): A in Boone, Campbell and Kenton; D0–D2 in the far-western New Madrid counties (e.g. McCracken, Fulton, Hickman D2).
KRC R507.2.2: deck girders may not bear on ledgers or band joists, and ledgers may not hang on stone or masonry veneer unless designed or using a listed fastening method.

counties.edition: 2018 IRC with Knox County amendments (Ordinance O-18-10-101, adopted Nov 19, 2018)
counties.wind_basis: As published in Knox County's Table R301.2(1) amendment ('90'); basis not stated; no topographic effects
deck_notes: Deck footings at least 12 in deep and 6 in thick, with two #4 bars each way at 6 in on center; size by beam, from 12x12 in square / 14 in round (2-2x6 or single beam) up to 24x24 in / 27 in round (2-2x12).

The ledger must be at least the joist size, fastened with 1/2 in lags or through-bolts staggered top to bottom: 30 in o.c. for joist spans up to 6 ft, down to 10 in o.c. for 16–18 ft. Never bolt to brick.

Guards at least 36 in where the deck is more than 30 in above grade; stair guards at least 34 in; openings must stop a 4 in sphere.
Stairs: max riser 7-3/4 in, min tread 10 in, nosing 3/4–1-1/4 in on treads under 11 in; a handrail is required on stairs with 4 or more risers; landings at least stair width x 36 in.
Lateral-load hold-down devices are required in at least two locations per deck (four with the alternate detail).
All fasteners, hangers and nails must be double hot-dipped galvanized or stainless steel.

counties.note: Values were read from the image of Fort Worth's Table R301.2(1) on page 6 of the ordinance. The table labels the wind speed '3-sec-gust' without saying ultimate or nominal, so confirm the design wind speed with the city before using it for uplift design.
